Running a Single PNU Analysis

Bill O’Brien

2026-10-29

Source: vignettes/SingleStudy.qmd

Overview

This vignette walks through a complete prevalent new-user (PNU) analysis. Code blocks show the full workflow using simulated data (no database required) and a database-backed workflow side by side. All code is correct and runnable in an R session with the package and its suggested dependencies installed.

Background

The PNU design conditions on how long a patient has been on the reference treatment (A) at the time of the index event (B). Patients who switch from A to B are the switchers (target cohort). Patients still on A are eligible comparators, indexed on the same day of their A therapy as the matched switcher. Groups of patients who share the same duration on A form exposure sets, and the time-conditional propensity score (TCPS) is estimated within those sets by conditional logistic regression.

Suissa S, Moodie EE, Dell’Aniello S. Prevalent new-user cohort designs for comparative drug effect studies by time-conditional propensity scores. Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2017;26(4):459–468. doi:10.1002/pds.4117

Step 1 — Simulate data

simulatePnuData() generates a synthetic cohort with a known true effect, making it useful for testing and method development. The true hazard ratio in the simulation below is 1.5.

library(PrevalentNewUser)

simArgs <- createSimulationArgs(
  nSwitchers         = 500L,
  nComparatorsPerSet = 500L,
  nExposureSets      = 3L,
  nCovariates        = 100L,
  outcomeBaseRate    = 0.15,
  logRr              = log(1.5),   # true HR = 1.5
  seed               = 42L
)

pnuData <- simulatePnuData(simArgs)
pnuData

Step 2 — Create study population

createStudyPopulation() applies eligibility criteria and attaches risk windows to the cohort. The result is stored as an Andromeda table inside pnuData.

spArgs <- createStudyPopulationArgs(
  outcomeId         = 1L,
  riskWindowStart   = 0L,
  riskWindowEnd     = 365L,
  endAnchor         = "cohort start",
  requireTimeAtRisk = FALSE
)

pnuData <- createStudyPopulation(pnuData, spArgs)

# Collect the study population into memory
pop <- dplyr::collect(pnuData$studyPopulation)
nrow(pop)

Step 3 — Fit the time-conditional propensity score

fitTcps() estimates the TCPS by conditional logistic regression (via Cyclops), stratified by exposure set. It returns the study population data frame with a propensityScore column added.

tcpsArgs <- createTcpsArgs()
pop <- fitTcps(pop, pnuData, tcpsArgs)

summary(pop$propensityScore)

Step 4 — Match on TCPS

matchOnTcps() performs nearest-neighbour matching within each exposure set.

matchArgs <- createMatchingArgs(
  maxRatio = 4L,
  caliper  = 0.2
)

matchedPop <- matchOnTcps(pop, matchArgs)

cat(sprintf(
  "Matched population: %d switchers, %d comparators\n",
  sum(matchedPop$treatment == 1L),
  sum(matchedPop$treatment == 0L)
))

Step 5 — Covariate balance

computeCovariateBalance() computes standardised mean differences (SMD) before and after matching. SMDs below 0.1 indicate adequate balance.

balArgs <- createBalanceArgs()
balance <- computeCovariateBalance(matchedPop, pnuData, balArgs)

# Show the five covariates with the largest absolute post-matching SMD
balance |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(afterMatchingSmd))) |>
  dplyr::select(covariate_name, beforeMatchingSmd, afterMatchingSmd) |>
  head(5)

Step 6 — Fit outcome model

fitOutcomeModel() fits a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model (via Cyclops) with the matched sets as strata.

omArgs <- createOutcomeModelArgs()
result <- fitOutcomeModel(matchedPop, pnuData, omArgs)

cat(sprintf(
  "HR = %.3f  (95%% CI %.3f–%.3f)\n",
  exp(result$logRr),
  result$ci95Lb,
  result$ci95Ub
))

Step 7 — Bootstrap confidence interval (optional)

bootstrapCi() replaces the Wald CI with a stratum-resampling bootstrap. Use this when the normal approximation is suspect (small matched sets, rare outcomes).

bsArgs   <- createBootstrapArgs(numberOfReplications = 500L, seed = 1L)
bsResult <- bootstrapCi(matchedPop, pnuData, omArgs, bsArgs)

cat(sprintf(
  "Bootstrap CI: %.3f–%.3f\n",
  bsResult$ci95Lb,
  bsResult$ci95Ub
))

Using the top-level orchestrator

For a full study with multiple analysis variants, runPnuAnalyses() handles iteration, error recovery, and file output:

analyses <- list(
  createPnuAnalysisArgs(
    analysisId          = 1L,
    description         = "primary (caliper 0.2)",
    studyPopulationArgs = spArgs,
    tcpsArgs            = tcpsArgs,
    matchingArgs        = matchArgs,
    outcomeModelArgs    = omArgs
  ),
  createPnuAnalysisArgs(
    analysisId          = 2L,
    description         = "sensitivity (no caliper)",
    studyPopulationArgs = spArgs,
    tcpsArgs            = tcpsArgs,
    matchingArgs        = createMatchingArgs(caliper = 0L, maxRatio = 4L),
    outcomeModelArgs    = omArgs
  )
)

outputFolder <- file.path(tempdir(), "pnu_demo")

summary <- runPnuAnalyses(
  pnuAnalysisList = analyses,
  outputFolder    = outputFolder,
  pnuDataList     = list(pnuData, pnuData)   # one entry per analysis; omit for DB workflow
)

summary[, c("analysis_id", "description", "log_rr", "status")]

Exporting results

exportToCsv() writes flat CSV files ready for Strategus aggregation or a Shiny results viewer.

exportFolder <- file.path(tempdir(), "pnu_export")

exportToCsv(
  outputFolder = outputFolder,
  exportFolder = exportFolder,
  databaseId   = "Synpuf_5pct"
)

list.files(exportFolder)

Empirical calibration (optional)

When negative control outcomes are available, use calibrateEstimates() to correct for residual systematic error before exporting.

# negativeControls must be a data frame with logRr and seLogRr columns
calibrated <- calibrateEstimates(
  estimates               = summary,
  negativeControlOutcomes = negativeControls
)

# Write the calibrated summary back and re-export
utils::write.csv(calibrated, file.path(outputFolder, "summary.csv"),
                 row.names = FALSE)
exportToCsv(outputFolder, exportFolder, databaseId = "Synpuf_5pct")

Database workflow

Running a PNU analysis against a real CDM database requires three steps before getDbPnuData(): define the cohorts with Capr, generate them with CohortGenerator, and then connect and load. Everything from Step 2 onwards is identical to the simulated-data workflow above.

Connecting to the database 

connectionDetails <- DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(
  dbms     = "postgresql",
  server   = "myserver/mydb",
  user     = Sys.getenv("DB_USER"),
  password = Sys.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")
)

cdmDatabaseSchema    <- "cdm"
cohortDatabaseSchema <- "results"
cohortTable          <- "pnu_cohorts"

Defining cohorts with Capr

This example implements a PNU study comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists (tirzepatide or semaglutide — treatment A, the reference) against bariatric surgery (treatment B, the switcher event). Patients must be 18 or older at cohort entry.

The GLP-1 RA cohort combines tirzepatide (concept 779705) and semaglutide (concept 793143) into a single concept set, so a patient enters the cohort at their first dispensing of either agent and exits when a 45-day gap in supply occurs. The 45-day persistence window accommodates monthly injectable formulations.

The bariatric surgery cohort is defined by a single procedure concept (4326683) and exits at the end of the patient’s observation period, since the index date is a one-time operative event.

library(Capr)

# --- Treatment A: GLP-1 receptor agonists (composite) -----------------------

glp1ra <- cs(
  descendants(779705L),   # tirzepatide
  descendants(793143L),   # semaglutide
  name = "GLP-1 receptor agonists"
)

glp1raCohort <- cohort(
  entry = entry(
    drugExposure(glp1ra, age(gte(18L))),
    primaryCriteriaLimit = "First"
  ),
  exit = exit(
    endStrategy = drugExit(glp1ra,
                           persistenceWindow  = 45L,
                           surveillanceWindow = 0L)
  )
)

# --- Treatment B: bariatric operative procedure -----------------------------

bariatricCs <- cs(
  descendants(4326683L),
  name = "Bariatric operative procedure"
)

bariatricCohort <- cohort(
  entry = entry(
    procedure(bariatricCs, age(gte(18L))),
    primaryCriteriaLimit = "First"
  ),
  exit = exit(
    endStrategy = observationExit()
  )
)

# Cohort IDs are assigned in order: 1 = GLP-1 RA, 2 = bariatric surgery
exposureCohorts <- makeCohortSet(glp1raCohort, bariatricCohort)

Generating cohorts with CohortGenerator 

library(CohortGenerator)

cohortTableNames <- getCohortTableNames(cohortTable = cohortTable)

createCohortTables(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTableNames     = cohortTableNames
)

generateCohortSet(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cdmDatabaseSchema    = cdmDatabaseSchema,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTableNames     = cohortTableNames,
  cohortDefinitionSet  = exposureCohorts
)

# Verify cohort counts
sql <- "SELECT cohort_definition_id, COUNT(*) AS n
        FROM @cohortDatabaseSchema.@cohortTable
        GROUP BY cohort_definition_id"
DatabaseConnector::renderTranslateQuerySql(
  connection           = DatabaseConnector::connect(connectionDetails),
  sql                  = sql,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTable          = cohortTable
)

Loading PNU data

The GLP-1 RA cohort is the reference treatment A (targetCohortId = 1), and the bariatric surgery cohort marks the switcher index dates (comparatorCohortId = 2). Exclude the GLP-1 RA concept IDs and their descendants from the covariates so the propensity model does not condition on the exposure itself.

covariateSettings <- FeatureExtraction::createDefaultCovariateSettings(
  excludedCovariateConceptIds   = c(779705L, 793143L),
  addDescendantsToExclude       = TRUE
)

pnuCohortArgs <- createPnuCohortArgs(
  targetCohortId     = 1L,   # GLP-1 RA (reference treatment A)
  comparatorCohortId = 2L,   # bariatric surgery (switcher / treatment B)
  outcomeCohortId    = 3L    # define and generate separately
)

pnuData <- getDbPnuData(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cdmDatabaseSchema    = cdmDatabaseSchema,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTable          = cohortTable,
  pnuCohortArgs        = pnuCohortArgs,
  covariateSettings    = covariateSettings
)

# Then proceed with Steps 2–7 or runPnuAnalyses() above

Storing results in a database

For multi-database studies, upload results to a shared results schema using the results data model functions.

resultsConnectionDetails <- DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(
  dbms   = "sqlite",
  server = "results.sqlite"
)

createResultsDataModel(resultsConnectionDetails, databaseSchema = "main")
uploadResults(resultsConnectionDetails, databaseSchema = "main",
              resultsFolder = outputFolder)
